answers.value: Requirements for the in-flight epic/feature under Business Analysis & Requirements Elaboration; scope = all user stories and acceptance criteria for the epic keyed by its Jira Epic link, plus the impacted Guidewire and integration touchpoints named in the epic charter.
Requirements elaboration window for the current PI/sprint; workshop date and the epic's target PI recorded on the Jira Epic and the Confluence requirements page header.

Every captured requirement has: unique ID, business rationale, INVEST-compliant story text, testable acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then), priority (MoSCoW), and a named business owner; stories missing acceptance criteria are flagged 'Needs Refinement' and excluded from ready-for-dev.

Number of requirements logged in Jira reconciles to the requirement count in the workshop notes and the requirements traceability matrix in Confluence (delta = 0); each maps to at least one business objective.

Workshop outputs (attendee list, decisions, requirement set) saved to the Confluence requirements space with page version and timestamp; recording/notes retained per project record policy (minimum 3 years).

Open questions and conflicting requirements logged as Jira issues labeled 'req-open-item' with owner and due date; parked items recorded in a decision log with disposition before stories are marked ready.

Elicitation approach/template version approved: use the standard requirements-workshop template v-current from the BA playbook in Confluence; version stamped on the page and agreed by the Product Owner before the session.
Sensitivity: requirements touching pricing, underwriting rules, or claims payout logic flagged 'high-impact' and require a second SME confirmation and Solution Architect review before acceptance.
Materiality: any requirement estimated >8 story points or crossing >2 systems is escalated to the Product Owner and Architecture for scope/feasibility sign-off before commit.
All requirements produced by the workshop (full set, no sampling) inspected against the definition-of-ready checklist in Jira.

PASS = 100% of committed stories have testable Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, a business owner, and traceability to a business objective; FAIL = any committed story missing acceptance criteria or owner.

Stories failing definition-of-ready are moved to 'Needs Refinement', a follow-up refinement session is scheduled within 5 business days, and they are excluded from the sprint until remediated (owner = Business Analyst).

Source-system field definitions confirmed against the data catalog/business glossary for any data element referenced (e.g., Guidewire PolicyCenter policy/coverage fields), with glossary term IDs cited in the story.
Where requirements assert data volumes or migration counts, source-system control totals are captured from the enterprise data warehouse and attached to the requirement as baseline figures.

Acceptance criteria: workshop notes signed off by the Product Owner, requirements traceability matrix complete with 0 orphan stories, and all high-impact items SME-confirmed; evidence location = Confluence requirements space (page version linked) and the Jira epic, cross-referenced in the traceability matrix.

All exit-criteria fields populated: 0 open blocker/critical defects, code coverage ≥ 80% on changed lines and ≥ 90% on critical paths, 100% of regression suite automated and passing, SAST/DAST with 0 critical/high findings (≤5 medium with waivers), performance within baseline SLA, and UAT sign-off attached.
Test execution counts reconcile: planned vs. executed test cases delta = 0 for mandatory suites; defect counts in the test-management tool match the Jira release defect query (blocker/critical = 0).

QA sign-off record (exit-criteria checklist, coverage report, security scan results, test summary report) exported to the compliance evidence repository, filename 'qa-signoff-<release>-<yyyymmdd>.pdf', with build SHA and reviewer signature; retained 7 years.

Any waived defect or accepted medium security finding logged as Jira issue type 'SDLC-Exception' with disposition and business justification, owner = Engineering Manager, 10-business-day remediation SLA; unresolved blockers/criticals veto sign-off.

Pre/post: full regression suite passes on the RC build with 0 new failures vs. the prior release baseline; performance benchmark within ±10% of the established baseline; no coverage regression on changed lines.
ServiceNow change/release record linked to the Jira release and the immutable build tag; references the QA sign-off evidence ID and the CI/CD pipeline run URL.
Go/No-Go decision (Approved / Conditional / Rejected) documented on the Jira release and in the release readiness review minutes in Confluence, with residual-risk statement and any conditions.

Sign-off distributed to Release Manager, Product Owner, DevOps Engineer, delivery squad, and Operations/Support via the Jira release comment and the #release-readiness Teams channel; recipient list captured in the review minutes.
The complete mandatory test scope for the RC build (unit, integration, contract, regression, security, performance) — no sampling; each suite's latest run tied to the build SHA.

PASS = 0 blocker/critical defects, coverage ≥ 80% changed / ≥ 90% critical paths, 100% regression green, 0 critical/high SAST/DAST findings, performance within SLA; FAIL = any unmet gate without an approved SDLC-Exception.

On FAIL, withhold sign-off and block deployment; open an SDLC-Exception (owner = Engineering Manager) for any risk-accepted item; only an approved conditional waiver with a dated remediation plan permits release.
In-scope period = the RC build's test-execution window; effective dates = the release's target deployment date recorded on the Jira release and the ServiceNow change record.
